newsitem.title: USA: Red Ant Records Sold to Venture Capital Firm.
newsitem.headline: Red Ant Records Sold to Venture Capital Firm.

text.p: Bankrupt music distributor Alliance Entertainment Corp. said Thursday it agreed to sell its nascent Red Ant Records label to venture capital firm Wasserstein Perella & Co.

Alliance will receive $625,000 in cash at closing and will retain a 10 percent equity interest in Red Ant, a statement said. Wasserstein Perella will also fund the Los Angeles-based label to the tune of at least $11 million, including a minimum of $3 million at closing.
New York-based Alliance, in which Wasserstein Perella has a minority stake, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on July 14.
Red Ant, whose acts include naked, Mexico 70 and Militia, was not included in the filing. Instead, investment bank Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette solicited bids for the label.
The deal is subject to a Bankruptcy Court hearing on Aug. 13, an Alliance spokesman said, and settlement is expected to take place soon afterwards.
Red Ant was founded last year by former MCA Music Entertainment chairman Al Teller with a reported $20 million backing from Wasserstein Perella. He named it after his initials, Alvin Norman Teller.

Teller later incorporated Red Ant into Alliance under a series of complex transactions designed to transform Alliance into a major music company. However, Alliance defaulted on its debts and sought bankruptcy protection. Teller resigned as chairman of Red Ant, but remains chairman of Alliance. The spokesman said Alliance expected to return to its core business as an independent music distributor.
